name: Ernesto And Fabio Bertarelli
current_role: Ernesto Bertarelli: head of B-FLEXION (formerly Waypoint Capital), Geneva; co-chair, Bertarelli Foundation
profile: 1997 Forbes entry for father and son behind Swiss biotech Serono. Fabio Bertarelli died in 1998; son Ernesto (b. 1965) ran Serono from 1996, shifted it to biotech and sold it to Merck KGaA in 2007 for $13.3bn. He now invests the family fortune via B-FLEXION and co-chairs the Bertarelli Foundation with sister Dona.
interesting_fact: Ernesto founded sailing team Alinghi, which won the America's Cup in 2003 on its first attempt, bringing the Cup to Europe for the first time; he was the team's only Swiss national, serving as navigator.
deep_cut_fact: The name Alinghi comes from the Bertarelli family boats that raced around Porto Santo Stefano and Porto Ercole on Monte Argentario, where Ernesto spent his youth sailing.
notes: Fabio Bertarelli (the father) died in 1998, so alive=unknown covers the pair: Ernesto is alive, Fabio is not. Profile focuses on Ernesto. The family site lists no published email. Best route is probably B-FLEXION in Geneva or the Bertarelli Foundation, whose marine-conservation work has protected over 3m km2 of ocean since 2010.

name: Vince McMahon
current_role: Founder of 14TH & I, a private sports, media and entertainment investment firm (Connecticut)
profile: Former WWE chairman and CEO. He bought his father's wrestling company in 1982 and built WWE into a global media business, which merged with UFC to form TKO in 2023. He resigned from TKO in January 2024 and in 2025 launched 14TH & I, named for the D.C. intersection where his father's Capitol Wrestling Corp. was based.
interesting_fact: McMahon was behind the 1976 Muhammad Ali vs. Antonio Inoki match, years before he took over his father's promotion.
deep_cut_fact: After graduating from East Carolina University in 1968 and working as a traveling salesman, he became a ring announcer in 1969. In 1971 he promoted his first card, in a small territory in Maine.
notes: Sensitive: he resigned from TKO in January 2024 amid a lawsuit alleging sexual misconduct, and in January 2025 he settled SEC charges over undisclosed payments (>$1.7m). Weigh reputational fit before any outreach. 14TH & I's site published no contact details; reported executives are Brad Blum (president) and David Spingarn (CIO), per https://wrestletalk.com/news/vince-mcmahon-new-company-wwe-exit-revealed/

name: Prakash Parmanand Hinduja
current_role: Chairman, Hinduja Group (Europe); Chairman of the Advisory Board, Hinduja Bank (Switzerland)
profile: Prakash 'PP' Hinduja is the third of the four Hinduja brothers behind the Hinduja Group, a conglomerate whose interests span Ashok Leyland, IndusInd Bank, Gulf Oil, energy and media. name: Sean Parker
current_role: Founder and chairman, Parker Foundation and Parker Institute for Cancer Immunotherapy; executive chairman of Stability AI (since 2024)

He became chairman of Stability AI in 2024.

name: Choo Chong Ngen
current_role: Founder, Worldwide Hotels Group (Hotel 81 and other brands), Singapore
profile: Singapore hotelier who made his first money in textiles, then launched the Hotel 81 budget chain in Geylang in 1995. His private Worldwide Hotels group, run with daughter Carolyn since 2002, has about 41 hotels in Singapore and has expanded since 2017 into Australia, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea and Thailand. name: Hubertus Benteler
current_role: Member of the supervisory board (former CEO), Benteler International AG, Salzburg
profile: Fourth-generation owner of Benteler International, which grew from Carl Benteler's 1876 ironware shop in Bielefeld into a roughly $9bn-revenue maker of automotive components, steel tubes and engineering equipment. He led the group from 1991, turning it into a global auto supplier, and moved to the supervisory board in 2017. Son Casper is expected to lead the family eventually.
interesting_fact: Benteler marks 150 years in 2026; the business began as a small ironware shop opened by Carl Benteler in Bielefeld, Germany, in 1876.
deep_cut_fact: Benteler's official timeline dates his era to 1991, when he took over management and remade the company into a global automotive partner. Its first Mexican plant opened in Puebla in 1992, and the Liberec (Czech) brownfield plant followed in 1995.
notes: Private family. Alive is inferred from Hurun Global 2026 and Forbes listings; no obituary was found. The press page loads its contacts dynamically, so no press email was captured. Corporate communications is the realistic route.

name: Basudeo Narain Singh
profile: Co-founder of Alkem Laboratories, one of India's largest pharma companies (incorporated 1973, listed on BSE/NSE), which he built with his elder brother Samprada Singh. Samprada, the Chairman Emeritus, has died; Basudeo is now Executive Chairman, and the next generation (e.g. MD Sandeep Singh) sits on the board.
interesting_fact: Alkem's own founders' story compares the two brothers' partnership to the Ramayana: 'a tale of two determined brothers' from Bihar who built a company now employing over 23,000 people.
deep_cut_fact: After the Jehanabad district school in Bihar and a degree from Patna University, he had started work as a professor when his brother called him into the business. In the early years he personally delivered stock to stockists and distributors.
notes: Listed as Executive Chairman on Alkem's board page (checked Nov 2026). Low media profile. Corporate head-office and IR channels are the published routes.

name: Rajiv Jain
current_role: Founder, Chairman and Chief Investment Officer, GQG Partners (Fort Lauderdale; ASX: GQG)
profile: India-born investor who came to the US in the early 1990s for an MBA at the University of Miami, joined Vontobel Asset Management in 1994 and became its co-CEO in 2014. In 2016 he co-founded GQG Partners with Tim Carver and listed it on the ASX in 2021; it now manages over US$150bn in long-only equities. He writes GQG's CIO Perspectives, which recently covered the AI investment cycle.

name: Yvonne Bauer
current_role: Owner and Chair of the Board, Bauer Media Group (Hamburg)
profile: Fifth-generation owner of Bauer Media Group, which grew from an 1875 printing shop into a European publishing, audio and outdoor-media group with hundreds of magazine titles (InTouch, Grazia) and over 400 websites and apps.
